reasons.plausibility: Scandium has a much lower melting point (1541 °C) than Hf (2233 °C) and is not refractory, making it highly unlikely to retain strength at 1000 °C in a single-phase BCC solid solution with Mo, Ta, Ti, Zr.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined rejection criterion (>10% strength drop or secondary phases), though the hypothesis is physically unsound.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes an element (Sc) that is fundamentally unsuitable for high-temperature refractory alloys, so testing it would waste resources.
